title: Quotient of two standard resolutions along an injective target map is a polynomial resolution
statement: Let $A\to B\xrightarrow{j}C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with $j$ injective. Let $P_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/A)$ and $Q_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(C/A)$ be the standard augmented simplicial polynomial algebras of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Use their standard functoriality map $P_\bullet\to Q_\bullet$ and the augmentation $P_\bullet\to B$ to form the simplicial $B$-algebra $\overline Q_\bullet=Q_\bullet\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$, with tensor products taken degreewise. The induced augmentation $\overline Q_\bullet\to C$ is a polynomial resolution: every $\overline Q_n$ is a polynomial $B$-algebra, every augmentation $\overline Q_n\to C$ is surjective, and $s(\overline Q_\bullet)\to C[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $B$-modules. Here $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$ has alternating-face differential and zero positive terms, as in the cited node. No flatness of $C$ over $B$, finiteness of the variable sets, or injectivity of $A\to B$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08SD, remark-triangle: the key fact that Q_bar = Q tensor_P B resolves C, and polynomiality from the injectivity of B to C. This is also the resolution input used in Tag 08SE, remark-explicit-map; no distinguished-triangle assertion is made here.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] for both standard resolutions and their functorial map $j_\bullet:P_\bullet\to Q_\bullet$. It gives augmentation compatibility, surjectivity $Q_n\to C$ in every degree, and quasi-isomorphisms $s(P)\to B[0]$, $s(Q)\to C[0]$. The simplicial augmentation $e:P_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}(B)$ also induces a quasi-isomorphism on alternating-face complexes: the map $s(\operatorname{const}(B))\to B[0]$ is the identity in degree zero and zero below, and its differential from degree $-n$ is the identity for positive even $n$ and zero for odd $n$. Thus its negative cohomology vanishes and its degree-zero cohomology is $B$. Its composite with $s(e)$ is the standard augmentation, so the assertion follows on cohomology.

source.place: Tags 08PM and 08PT (standard resolution); Tag 08SD (remark-triangle), choice of P and Q; the elementary alternating complex of a constant simplicial module

proof.text: Put $P_{-1}=B$, $Q_{-1}=C$, $j_{-1}=j$. Induct on $n\geq0$, assuming $j_{n-1}$ injective (the initial assumption is precisely the given injectivity). The standard formula makes $j_n:A[UP_{n-1}]\to A[UQ_{n-1}]$ send $[p]$ to $[j_{n-1}(p)]$. Put $E_n=UQ_{n-1}\setminus j_{n-1}(UP_{n-1})$. By the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], there are inverse maps $P_n[X_e:e\in E_n]\leftrightarrows Q_n$: coefficients $[p]$ go to $[j_{n-1}(p)]$ and $X_e$ to $[e]$; inversely an image variable $[j_{n-1}(p)]$ goes to $[p]$ and a complementary variable to $X_e$, fixing $A$. Their composites fix every generator and every coefficient. Evaluating the complementary variables at zero retracts the coefficient inclusion $P_n\to P_n[E_n]$, so $j_n$ is injective. This completes the induction and identifies $Q_n$ as a polynomial $P_n$-algebra in each degree.

source.place: Tag 08SD (remark-triangle), polynomiality of Q_n over P_n from injectivity; the maps are written using the polynomial universal property

proof.text: In the polynomial description from Step 2, the monomials in $E_n$ form a $P_n$-module basis: each polynomial is uniquely a finite linear combination of them. Hence $Q_n$ is free as a $P_n$-module. The explicit free-module clause of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] implies that $Q_n$ is flat over $P_n$. This holds for every $n$, with no finiteness restriction on $E_n$.

source.place: Tag 08SD (remark-triangle), flatness of Q_n over P_n; free monomial basis and the general free-implies-flat lemma

proof.text: Degreewise tensor and the augmentation define the simplicial $B$-algebra $\overline Q$ and the map $\bar\epsilon:\overline Q\to C$: in degree $n$ it is $q\otimes b\mapsto\epsilon_Q(q)j(b)$. This is balanced because $\epsilon_Q(j_n(p))=j(\epsilon_P(p))$, and commutes with every simplicial operator by augmentation compatibility. The map $P_n[E_n]\otimes_{P_n}B\to B[E_n]$ sends $\sum_\alpha p_\alpha X^\alpha\otimes b$ to $\sum_\alpha\epsilon_P(p_\alpha)bX^\alpha$. Its inverse sends $bX^\alpha$ to $X^\alpha\otimes b$; the tensor balancing relation and uniqueness of polynomial coefficients show both composites are identities [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Thus $\overline Q_n$ is a polynomial $B$-algebra. Given $c\in C$, choose $q\in Q_n$ with $\epsilon_Q(q)=c$ using Step 1; then $\bar\epsilon_n(q\otimes1)=c$. Thus every augmentation is surjective.

source.place: Tag 08SD (remark-triangle), Q_bar = Q tensor_P B; degreewise polynomial base change and induced augmentation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-simplicial-flat-base-change-quasi-iso] with $R_\bullet=P_\bullet$, $S_\bullet=\operatorname{const}(B)$, $f=e$, and $M_\bullet=Q_\bullet$ via $j_\bullet$. The ring-map hypothesis was verified in Step 1 and degreewise flatness in Step 3; the operators on $Q$ are semilinear because $j_\bullet$ is a simplicial ring map. Consequently $s(Q)\to s(\overline Q)$, $q\mapsto q\otimes1$, is a quasi-isomorphism of underlying abelian-group complexes. Its composite with $s(\bar\epsilon):s(\overline Q)\to C[0]$ is $s(Q)\to C[0]$, already a quasi-isomorphism by Step 1. On every cohomology group this says $H(\bar\epsilon)$ composed with an isomorphism is an isomorphism; hence $H(\bar\epsilon)$ is an isomorphism. Finally $\bar\epsilon$ is $B$-linear, and the kernels, images and quotients defining its cohomology have the same underlying groups after forgetting $B$. A bijective $B$-linear map has a $B$-linear inverse, so it is a quasi-isomorphism of $B$-module complexes as required. Together with Step 4 this gives all clauses of a polynomial resolution.
